protocol:
American Society for Microbiology's Gelatin Hydrolysis Test Protocol (Dela Cruz and Torres 2012). 
  
 Test tubes filled prepared with nutrient gelatin were inoculated by stabbing a sterile needle with the target isolate. Tubes were then incubated at 28°C for 2 days; to confirm liquefaction due to gelatinase activity, tubes were immersed in ice for 15-30 minutes then removed and tilted to observe for hydrolysis even after the ice bath.
sample_site_description: Under redwood trees covered by loose organic matter such as pines, vines and decomposing leaves.

protocol:
Adapted nitrate test protocol provided by Dr. González-Orta. 
  
 Test tubes with durham tubes filled with prepared nitrate were inoculated using a sterile loop to transfer a target isolate until turbid. Utilizing a modified procedure, 1-mL of liquid isolate culture was pipetted into a new 1.5-mL tube. Two drops of reagent A (sulfanilic acid) and reagent B (⍺-naphthylamine) are added. A change in color indicated nitrate reduction while gas in the original durham tube indicated denitrification.

 2. Check Durham tube for bubble formation (denitrification, N2 gas production) vs. no bubble (no denitrification, no N2 gas). 
 3. Aliquot 1000 uL of inoculated nitrate broth into an Eppendorf tube.  
 4. Add 2 drops of reagent A (sulfanilic acid), then 2 drops of reagent B (alpha-naphthylamine).  
 5. Observe for immediate red color change (nitrate reduction) vs. delayed or no color change (no nitrate reduction).

Protocol: 
 Inoculate a tube of SIM media using an inoculating wire or needle. Pick a bacterial colony with a sterile inoculating wire and stab straight down through the agar towards the bottom of the tube and quickly withdraw the wire along the same path. Do not move the wire around in the agar. 
 Sterilize the wire with a flame after each inoculation. 
 For control, repeat steps 1-2 with sterile needle 
 Incubate the tubes at the optimal growth temperature (25ºC) for 5 days. 
 Examine the tubes for evidence of hydrogen sulfide production (browning or blackening of the media). Record the results. 
 Examine the tubes for evidence of motility, cloudiness or turbidity of the media that extends outside of the stab line into the surrounding agar. Nonmotile bacteria will only exhibit growth in the stab line.  
 After recording your sulfide and motility results, test for indole by adding 1-2 ml of Kovac’s reagent to the SIM tube. Indole is present if a cherry red color develops on the surface of the culture medium. 
 Record your data in the chart. Include a photo of your SIM tubes.

protocol:
1. Obtain enough blood agar plates for my samples and divide the plates into two sections so one bacteria is on one side and another is on the other side. 
 2. Label the bottom of the plates (both sides) with initials, date, and bacteria/number. (One bacteria will be on one side and a different one on the other side, so label them separately.) 
 3. Use a sterile toothpick to touch a bacterial colony to transfer it to the plate. 
 4. Streak the sample into the corresponding section by moving the toothpick back and forth (like tri-streaking, just only the first streak.) Make sure to keep the samples in their designated area and don't get too close to the other section to avoid cross-contamination. 
 5. Repeat these steps for the other plates and bacteria samples. Be sure to use a new toothpick every time. 
 6. Store your plates agar side up and leave them to inoculate until next class.

protocol:
1. Label test tubes containing agar medium with initials, date, sample to be tested, and agar type. (motility test medium, motility - indole - lysine) 
 2. Using the stick with the thin, long metal on the end, heat it over the Bunsen burner until it turns orange, so that it cleans it and kills any bacteria on it.  
 3. Let it cool and then pick up a single colony from the sample being used. Stick the end of the metal about halfway down into the semi-solid agar medium.  
 4. Pull it straight out of the medium to keep the same line as it entered the medium. 
 5. Incubate/grow the test tubes at 35 degrees C for 18 hours until growth is evident. Can incubate for up to 7 days. Repeat these steps for all bacteria samples.  
 6. Observe the test tubes carefully and look for signs of growth.  
 7. Be sure to let the metal cool before collecting a bacteria sample so it doesn't kill the bacteria. 
 8. Be sure to heat the metal between every use of a different bacteria sample.
